_readme.authority: PHP is normative. This file is not a specification of the resolver — it is the resolver's own output, captured. A divergence found by scripts/conformance.mjs is a bug in lib/resolve.mjs until proven otherwise. Never edit a case to make the script pass: that inverts the authority and the whole arrangement stops meaning anything.
_readme.scope_keys: Contexts are recorded in BUSINESS KEYS (language code, market code, product name) and never uuids — every knowledge entity mints Uuid::v4(), so a case pinned to an id would stop matching the day someone reloads fixtures.
_readme.hashing: prompt_sha256 and dropped_sha256 are recorded for every case; the full prompt and drop list only for the first verbose_cases entries. Recording both in full for every case produced a 40MB file, which the target git repository cannot carry per bundle version. A hash catches a divergence just as well — it only cannot show it. Use unima:knowledge:explain for the full detail of one context.
_readme.as_of: The effective-window filter is evaluated at the recorded instant, derived from the corpus (the latest effective_from, UTC) rather than from the clock. An unanchored export would resolve against the wall clock and produce a different tree on a different day.
